script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

We open on JAMES (30s, ambitious, determined), sitting in the dimly lit living room, poring over business plans.

JAMES
(muttering to himself)
If this works... if it all comes together... I'll finally be able to make a difference.

INT. JAMES'S OFFICE - DAY

James sits at his desk, surrounded by stacks of paperwork and business files. The phone rings. He answers it.

JAMES
James Thompson speaking.

ANNE (40s, competent, no-nonsense)
James, this is Anne at the city planning commission. I've got some good news and some bad news for you.

James leans forward, his eyes narrowing.

JAMES
Give me the bad news first.

Anne hesitates, then delivers the news.

ANNE
The zoning restrictions on your proposed development site have been changed. It's no longer zoned for commercial use.

James's face falls.

JAMES
What about the good news?

Anne's tone softens.

ANNE
Well, there is an alternative site nearby that's available. It's not ideal, but it's the best option you have right now.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James sits across from ANNA (20s, passionate, creative), a young architect he's been dating for a few months. He looks dejected.

ANNA
What's wrong? You seem distracted.

JAMES
(sighs)
My proposed development site got rezoned. Now I have to start all over again.

Anna looks sympathetic.

ANNA
I know how much you've been working on that. It's a setback, but it's not the end of the world.

James looks at her, a glint of determination in his eyes.

JAMES
No, it's not. But I can't afford to lose momentum. I need to find a new site, fast.

INT. ANNE'S OFFICE - DAY

James enters Anne's office, his mind made up.

JAMES
Anne, I've got a proposal for you. I want to buy that alternative site you mentioned.

Anne looks surprised.

ANNE
But James, it's not a commercial site. It's zoned for residential use.

JAMES
I understand that, but I believe I can make it work. I've got a vision for that site, and I won't let a little zoning restriction stand in my way.

Anne looks skeptical, but intrigued.

ANNE
Alright, James. Let's see what you can do.

INT. JAMES'S OFFICE - NIGHT

James sits at his desk, pouring over maps and blueprints, determined to make the residential site work for his commercial development.

INT. COUNCIL CHAMBERS - DAY

James stands before the city council, making his case for the residential-to-commercial zoning change. The council members are skeptical, but James remains calm and persuasive.

COUNCIL MEMBER 1 (50s, skeptical, cautious)
Mr. Thompson, we understand your ambition, but this is a risky proposition. Are you prepared to handle the potential backlash from the community?

James nods confidently.

JAMES
Yes, I am. I've consulted with local architects, engineers, and urban planners. We have a plan that will benefit the community and make this development a success.

The council members exchange glances, then vote unanimously in favor of the zoning change.

INT. JAMES'S OFFICE - DAY

James sits at his desk, surrounded by cheering employees and contractors, as they celebrate the successful zoning change and the green light for the development project.

JAMES
(raising a glass)
To new beginnings, and to making a difference in this city.

FADE OUT.

The end.
